Item 7 provides that the regulations will supersede the regulations in EO 8748 of May 1, 1941 and "shall become effective on July 1, 1942". It is a timing and replacement provision: the regulations took effect and superseded the EO 8748 regulations on July 1, 1942, which completed it. Its end is recorded at the stated effective date (July 1, 1942), with the later supersession of all of EO 9155's regulations by EO 9252 on October 9, 1942 as a later event, which cannot be an earlier end of a command already performed.

research_rationale:
EO 9155 (7 FR 3277, signed 1942-05-01) approves Civil Service Commission regulations on efficiency-rating boards of review, effective July 1, 1942. The clause inventory has eleven clauses: items 1, 2, 3(a) to 3(e), 4, 5, 6 and 7. EO 9252 (7 FR 8079, signed 1942-10-09) superseded the regulations in EO 9155 in its item 8 and made them effective immediately (the Federal Register text reads "effective immediately" with a soft hyphen in the held bytes), so items 1 to 6 ended on 1942-10-09 by express supersession. Item 7, which makes the regulations effective on July 1, 1942 and supersedes the EO 8748 regulations, was performed on that date; the EO 9252 supersession is a later event for it. The whole-order end is the latest clause end, 1942-10-09. The bounded searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register disposition notes) show no other later instrument.

savings.reason: Rating adjustments and board decisions made under the regulations between July 1 and October 9, 1942 are accrued results. EO 9252 provides that only its own successor-service provision operates retroactively (to July 1, 1941); it contains no clause keeping EO 9155 alive after supersession.
